attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: This is a retrospective observation with two parts: GPT-5 was not released that week, and many had hoped it would be. The normalised wording keeps both parts and the 'this week' scope.

contract.note: Reading the week as Aug 12–18, 2024 and 'drop' as a public release is the ordinary reading. Requiring evidence of the 'many had hoped' clause is fair, since the speaker asserted it. Asking that GPT-5 hopes be told apart from Strawberry speculation is reasonable.

evidence.note: OpenAI's model release notes show only a GPT-4o update on Aug 12, described as not a new frontier model. The next entry is dated Sep 3. This supports non-release during the week.
Commentary dated Aug 16 treats GPT-5 as not yet released. It backs the non-release part. Its own prediction about future releases is not used.
Aug 15 coverage expects a frontier model soon but says it may not be called GPT-5. It does not show hopes for a GPT-5 release specifically that week.
OpenAI introduced GPT-5 on Aug 7, 2025. That fits non-release in 2024, but it falls outside the target period, so it counts as context only.

reviews.rationale: The non-release part is well supported: OpenAI's Aug 12 entry describes a GPT-4o update, not a new frontier model, and the Aug 16 commentary treats GPT-5 as unreleased. The contract also requires evidence of noticeable hopes for GPT-5 that week. The packet shows only general frontier-model speculation that was unsure of the name and timing (e3). Nothing contradicts the clause, but nothing establishes it either. Because the support condition is only half met, the result is unresolved.
